title: H1 Free machinery: response-shape changes derived from existing state
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. This sprint attacks the two biggest waste classes (poll-after-mutate, retry-on-terminal-error) purely by changing what existing commands return. No new schema, no new enforcement risk; every task derives its payload from state the ledgers already record. Ships independently of the lane isolation plan.
acceptanceCriteria: Every task closed with test evidence and a commit SHA
No new ledger record types introduced by this sprint
closedReason: Sprint scope completed for runtime hardening milestone.
